title: Ghassan and the River That Argued
logline: Ghassan fights Wahhaj until they discover they were always the same water.
story: Certain they were opposites and enemies, Ghassan, who carried the vigor of youth, ran headlong against Wahhaj, who was the burning, blazing one. Each tried to push the other back uphill, and they struggled until both were spent and still. In that stillness Ghassan noticed they had pooled together and could no longer tell which water had been which. What Ghassan had fought so hard in Wahhaj was only the part of Ghassan that had never been lived. Joined, they became a river wide enough to carry them both.
moral: What you fight hardest in another is most often the unlived part of yourself.
